A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GLOV, with matching core methods and recognition experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original recognition experiments, prompt-transfer evaluations, and guidance ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains original recognition results and adds safety evaluations, reduced-label and model-scaling experiments, and repeated-run results.

M1.justification: The ranked-prompt search, history buffer, sentence embeddings, and hidden-state guidance remain unchanged. v6 adds a task-specific adaptation using attack-success-rate reduction as fitness and optimizing safety instructions prepended to VLM inputs (Sections 3.1 and 4.2).

E1.justification: v6 retains the recognition datasets, FOCI multiple-choice classification, and SST-5 probing. It adds MM-Safety-Bench and VLGuard safety tasks involving harmful images/instructions and benign controls, plus SEED and MME evaluations of general capabilities. These substantially expand task and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: v6 removes the Meta-Prompt comparator from the LLaVA recognition comparison in Table 2. The earlier CoOp comparison is expanded with LoRA applied to all matrices or only attention blocks (v6 Table 10), while its DTD and Caltech101 columns disappear. New safety comparisons include unprotected and initial-safety-instruction baselines for LLaVA-OV and Molmo.

E3.justification: New protocols include safety optimization on 50 VLGuard samples, transfer across models and benchmarks, refusal/GPT-4 judging, class-subset optimization, and a Llama-3.1-70B optimizer configuration. The stated LLaVA budget also changes from 50 iterations, except 25 for 1,000-class datasets, to 25 generally. Identical retained scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v6 adds analyses of optimization with labels from only a subset of classes, larger-LLM optimization, safety-prompt transfer, and preservation of general capabilities (Tables 3–6). Earlier guidance-design, layer-selection, prompt-transfer, multiple-choice, and five-shot analyses remain, with several moved to Appendix B.

E5.justification: v3 provides point estimates and optimization trajectories without repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v6 Appendix B.5/Table 11 adds a limited check using five random GLOV runs on four CLIP datasets, with ± quantities described as variances. It asserts statistical significance without specifying a formal test.

E6.justification: Shared recognition scores in Tables 1 and 2 remain numerically unchanged, but comparator entries are removed and substantial new results appear. For example, v6 Table 3 reports LLaVA VLGuard Safe-Unsafes ASR of 61.8% for the baseline and 1.1% for GLOV. Tables 4–6 and 10–15 add reduced-label, scaling, capability-retention, LoRA, repeated-run, and detailed safety outcomes.

T1.justification: The classification-fitness, sentence-embedding, guidance-update, and encoder-decoder prediction equations remain mathematically unchanged (Equations 1–6). Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v6 adds no substantive mathematical derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: v6 retains the recognition-improvement claims but expands the abstract and introduction to VLM safety, claiming ASR reductions up to 60.7 percentage points with minimal generalization degradation. Section 2.2 also introduces a novelty claim about optimizing VLM safety instructions without human intervention.

C2.justification: v6 adds interpretations concerning safety-prompt transfer, preservation of general capabilities, and possible benefits from closer attention to instructions. It discusses generalization to unseen classes, future unsupervised fitness signals, and propagation of LLM biases into VLM behavior. These materially expand applicability and limitation discussions beyond v3.

D1.justification: v6 adds exact safety and 70B-generated prompts, clarifies held-out-data selection of the guidance scale, and corrects prompt-list indexing in Algorithm 1. It adds statements about a code.zip supplement and README instructions, while v3's front-page project link disappears. Actual external code availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to PEFT and prompt-tuning approaches, including DePT, LoPA, LoRA/QLoRA, and adapters, alongside VLM safety research. v6 explicitly positions dataset-level natural-language prompts against category-level and continuous-prompt methods and adds safety-specific novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v6 substantially restructures the narrative and appendices, rewrites related-work and baseline discussions, and replaces much of the meta-prompt terminology with LLM prompt. Transfer and multiple-choice analyses move from the main text into an organized ablation appendix, while the main narrative now covers recognition and safety.

P2.justification: v6 adopts a different journal layout, typography, text width, and table-caption placement. Figure 2 adds a legend distinguishing optimization flow and helper inputs. New safety, ablation, and uncertainty tables substantially expand the displays, while existing generalization tables are relocated and reformatted. Most earlier plots and prompt-evolution figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 substantially strengthens evidence for GLOV's generality and practical reliability through safety transfer with capability-retention controls, reduced-label experiments, and repeated-run analysis. These address important questions left open in v3 and outweigh the removed Meta-Prompt comparison. Reporting weaknesses remain: unchanged recognition scores accompany an unexplained iteration-budget revision, and statistical significance is asserted without a specified test. The new safety results also document some capability losses (Tables 3 and 6), qualifying the broader benefits.
